title: RCP Core v1
description: Universal recipe protocol — core layer. Category profiles extend this additively via allOf; a profile may add fields and tighten constraints but may never remove or redefine a core field, so a core-only consumer can always render any RCP document correctly if incompletely.

rcp.description: Protocol major version. Required at the document root; omitted on nested components.

difficulty.description: Asserted facet (DECISIONS #10; PRD-002 OQ-3): integer 1..5. Source books using coarser scales (1–3 chef hats) map in per-ingest; the mapping call is recorded in provenance notes, never guessed silently.

bases.description: Named quantities that ratios are expressed relative to. This is what generalizes baker's percentage to every domain.

components.description: Sub-recipes whose output is an ingredient of the parent. May be of a different `kind` than the parent — this is why the core must be shared across profiles. Each entry is either an INLINE recipe (one-off element) or a REFERENCE to any published recipe by id (shared building block: ganache, stock, syrup). There is no special 'base recipe' type — being a base is curation (packs, kind: component), not essence.

maintenance.description: Component-level: a recurring culture (massa-mãe, SCOBY, lievito madre) that survives the recipe rather than being consumed by it.

min_batch.description: Component-level: minimum viable batch — scaling the parent may not shrink this component below it (you cannot build 3 g of levain).

carried_over.description: Component-level: backslopped — the output of batch N-1 is the input of batch N (massa velha, kombucha starter liquid).

derived.description: Values the app computes rather than the author states: final ABV from components + dilution, extraction yield from dose/yield/TDS, OG/FG to ABV.

options.description: Author-declared choices that reshape the method (autolise on/off, double vs single fermentation). Optional steps are NOT deletions — each option selects between fully-authored alternative paths via step guards, so every path is reviewed and testable. Downstream steps anchor on produced intermediates, not step ids, so whichever path is active satisfies the DAG.

times.description: Recipe-level time metadata (DS-PR-005; research 04:79-80). `active` (hands-on) and `total` are deliberately separate fields — same total, opposite effort (stir-fry vs risotto). Each value is a duration window; single book values encode as `target`. Closed object: a new phase name is a schema change, not authoring freedom.

storage.description: Storage guidance (DS-PR-007). An array because book pages routinely give multiple conditions (days airtight at room, months frozen). `where` is a closed enum; free-text nuance goes in `container`/`note`.

version.description: Revision number of THIS document, pinned by componentRef.version at reference sites. HARDENED (P8 triage): componentRef always pinned a version, but no field existed for the target to declare one — the gap the brownie→ganache defect exposed.

profile.description: Category-specific extension block. Validated by the profile schema selected by `kind`.

^x-.description: Vendor extension bucket. Consumers MUST ignore and MUST preserve unknown x- fields on round-trip.

componentRef.description: A component included by reference to another recipe document. Rules: (1) only `published` recipes may be referenced — a draft ref is a validation warning; (2) `version` pins the referenced revision, so editing the ganache never silently changes every brownie; (3) at publish/bundle time the ref is RESOLVED and the component embedded (SPEC-006: delivered snapshots are self-contained for offline), keeping ref+version as lineage; (4) the validator rejects reference cycles.

id.description: Local alias used by `ingredients[].component` and step `uses`/`after` in THIS recipe.

ref.description: Id of the referenced recipe document.

version.description: Pinned revision of the referenced recipe. Omit only in authoring; publish resolves and pins.

draw.description: How much of the referenced recipe's yield this parent consumes ('makes 500 g, use 200 g'). The scaler sizes the component batch from this, respecting the child's min_batch.

overrides.description: Reference-site adjustments ('this brownie's ganache uses 70% chocolate') expressed with the same substitution ops, scoped to the referenced component. Large divergence should fork a variant instead — same promotion rule as D8c.

text.description: Prose. Either a bare string in the document's `lang`, or a locale map. Prose is permitted ONLY where the sole consumer is a human eye — anything the renderer, scaler, substitution engine or safety checker reads must be an enum or a registry reference.

kind.description: CLOSED ENUM. Selects the profile schema. Adding a category is a new profile file, not a change to core.

role.description: CLOSED ENUM. The functional role an ingredient plays. Substitution matches on roles, not names — which is why egg (binder + leavener + emulsifier + moisture + colourant) has no drop-in replacement.

quantity.description: TAGGED UNION. A bare number cannot honestly hold every domain's quantities.

oneOf.title: parts
oneOf.description: Dimensionless until instantiated at a chosen target. A Negroni is genuinely 1:1:1 with no absolute quantities.

variant.description: Never scales. `to_consistency` (choux egg) additionally carries a non-binding guide and a sensory endpoint, because the true amount is not knowable in advance.

unit.description: TWO TIERS. `convertible` units map to UCUM and support exact arithmetic. `discrete` units are only ever multiplied, never converted — and the list is registry-backed, not frozen, because a closed unit enum (Crouton's mistake) cannot add a regional unit without a client update. Weight/volume conversion is per-ingredient via catalog density, never assumed 1 g = 1 ml.

scalingBehaviour.description: CLOSED ENUM. A single global multiplier is wrong in every domain. `area` covers pan geometry (r², so 20cm→23cm is ~1.32x, not 1.15x).

item.description: REGISTRY REFERENCE into the ingredient-class catalog (e.g. ingredient.flour.wheat.t65). Recipes reference a class, never a purchasable product — the shopping layer resolves class to product. HARDENED (SR-PR-002/DS-PR-003): null is schema-valid and marks an unresolved import (freshly-ingested, not yet mapped) — the semantic linter WARNS on null, the schema never errors; `raw` always survives for audit and re-parsing.

component.description: This ingredient is produced by the named component.

removed_after.description: Step id. For cultures/SCOBYs/aromatics present during the process but removed rather than consumed — excluded from final nutrition.

proposed_class.description: Extraction's proposed canonical ENGLISH class for an unresolved item (item: null) — the gap ledger groups by this so cross-language raws (cebola/onion) consolidate under one mint candidate (SR-REG-005). Never a mint; a proposal for the steward.

raw.description: Original text as scraped or extracted. Preserved for audit and re-parsing even after canonical resolution.

constraint.description: Bounded quantity. A `critical` constraint may not be violated by scaling or substitution — the engine must refuse and explain, not silently produce an unsafe recipe. HARDENED (SR-PR-002): at least one bound is required — a constraint without bounds is not a constraint; ratio bounds require `of` naming the basis they are ratios of.

duration.description: A window, never a bare number — lamination rests, cold retard and macaron skinning all fail on BOTH sides.

temperature.description: FOUR SHAPES: scalar; band with tolerance (crème anglaise 80-84C, where 86C is scrambled); a registry-backed named stage (sugar work, with fuzzy source-dependent boundaries); or a curve of waypoints (chocolate tempering: melt to cool to rework, all three differing by chocolate type).

endpoint.description: How you know it is ready. CLOSED ENUM on `kind`. Multiple endpoints coexist — '96C core OR hollow when tapped' is how people actually bake. Sensory endpoints are where per-step media earns its place; 'smells lactic, not putrid' resists numeric encoding entirely.

trigger.description: When a scheduled event fires. FOUR SHAPES, one union: elapsed (V60 pour at 0:45), remaining (hop addition 20 min before boil-end), recurring (fold every 30min x4; burp daily), and measurement-triggered (rack when SG < 1.005 — no calendar date at all).

primitive.description: REGISTRY REFERENCE, versioned. Follows SPEC-008's rule: a new capability is a new id, never a repurposed one; params only ever grow optionally.

after.description: Step ids, component ids, OR produced-intermediate ids this depends on. Anchoring on an intermediate (massa-misturada) rather than a step id is what lets guarded alternative paths coexist: whichever active step `produces` it satisfies the dependency. OMIT for simple sequential order — the DAG is opt-in.

section.description: Named method section this step belongs to (mistura, fermentacao, cozedura). Sections are the unit method-level substitutions can replace wholesale.

params.description: Primitive-specific parameters (SPEC-008 paramValues): lamination geometry, fold type, pour weight. Validated by the primitive's ParamSpec in the registry, not by core.

cues.description: Troubleshooting: if you observe X, do Y. Structured, not buried in prose.

recoverable.description: False for irreversible failures like over-mixed macaronage.

guard.description: Conditional content. A step or ingredient is active only when the guard matches the currently selected options. This ONE mechanism serves substitution deltas, equipment branches, execution modes and dietary transforms — four things four domain tracks independently asked for.

option.description: Matches when the named toggle option is on, or 'id:value' for a choice option.

role.description: `failure` matters: kahm yeast vs mould is a photo, not a sentence.

licence.description: REQUIRED. This project runs two tiers deliberately: written heritage CC BY 4.0, media all rights reserved. A media model without a licence field quietly erases that.

ref.description: Registry reference to an equipment profile document.

required.description: False where the equipment is a convenience; true where it is a feasibility gate (brioche at 60% butter, Italian meringue).

substitutes.description: Swapping these triggers a method delta via the same mechanism as ingredient substitution.

substitution.description: Substitution targets are NOT only ingredients. `scope` says what is being swapped: an ingredient slot, a piece of equipment, one or more steps, a whole named section of the method (hand-knead vs mixer vs no-knead folds; steam vs bake), or an entire component sub-recipe (levain -> commercial-yeast prep). Method-level substitutions use `with_steps`; everything else uses `with`.

with_steps.description: Replacement steps when scope is steps/section. Must produce the same intermediate (`produces`) as the replaced ones so downstream steps still resolve.

formula.description: Closed arithmetic grammar, never eval. E.g. hop substitution by alpha-acid units.

class.description: What else must be recomputed or warned about. `compensation-forcing`: one swap requires correlated additions (NA spirit needs added acid + tannin).

executionMode.description: The same recipe executed differently. Dilution is the canonical case: water that ice contributes for free to a stirred drink must become an explicit measured ingredient when batching, or the batch is ~20% over-strength.

loss.description: Fractional loss between raw and finished, e.g. baker's loss ~0.12.

variable.description: True where yield genuinely cannot be predicted, e.g. oleo saccharum.

provenance.description: First-class, and disagreement is data. Almost nobody else models this; for a heritage archive it is the whole point.

work.description: Publication/book title (DS-PR-008) — the work the page reference points into.

page.description: Page reference as a string: admits '123', '123-125', 'xii' (DS-PR-008).

divergences.description: Recorded disagreements between sources, deliberately left unresolved.

import.description: Ingestion metadata. Capture loosely, resolve canonically later, never block on perfect identity resolution. Imported recipes land unverified — for this archive an import is a lead, not a publication.

unresolved.description: Paths the extractor could not resolve to registry values. It emits null and keeps `raw`; it never invents.
